prompt: Prototype a pricing page in code so we can click through it.
assertions: The coded artifact is explicitly labeled disposable, design-reference, or production-candidate.
It is not presented as production-ready; the note that engineering, accessibility, and quality review are still required is present.
It states the register and a one-line design read.
Findings are presented as a Before/After/Why table.
Each finding carries a severity rank.
The review closes with a binary go/no-go verdict.
Any appearance claim is backed by the rendered evidence; if no build was viewed it states 'code-level pass, not an art review' instead of signing off on appearance.

prompt: Build a color system for light and dark mode.
assertions: Tokens are expressed as exact OKLCH values, not adjectives.
Contrast is verified against the stated floors and the result is reported.
A dark-mode ramp is included alongside the light ramp.

prompt: Design the states for a search input with async results.
assertions: The spec covers the full state set: default, hover, focus, active, disabled, loading, error, success, plus empty for every data region.
Real content at realistic lengths is used — the longest realistic string, the empty case, and the overflow case.
Exact values are specified rather than adjectives.

prompt: Hand off the approved onboarding screens to frontend.
assertions: A per-screen spec plus tokens and a motion plan is provided.
A handoff.yaml companion is included.
Artifact paths, owners, and constraints are recorded without duplicating the full artifact.

prompt: Generate six section illustrations for our SaaS landing page that all look like one family.
assertions: The strategy is named as consistency: one engine, anchored, serial — not a parallel fan-out across engines.
The hero (most-scrutinized slot) is generated first as the anchor and gated against DESIGN.md before the rest; downstream slots use it as a reference image, each at its own ratio.
A curation pass scores every image on on-brand, consistency, slot-fit, and technical, and regenerates only failing slots.
Per-asset provenance is recorded (generated vs captured, slot, prompt, model, date).

prompt: Review this faithful rebuild of our old site against the original screenshots before we hand it to the client.
assertions: The change mode is named as reproduce and the rubric is fidelity to the source screenshot, section by section.
Anti-default findings are marked advisory, not blocking, in reproduce mode.
Accessibility floors stay blocking in reproduce mode; a source that fails them is reported, not reproduced silently.
Any image slot that would need a real person, product, place, or work of the business stays a real photo or a placeholder; no generated stand-in is proposed.
The output is a Before/After/Why table with a binary verdict, and states 'code-level pass, not an art review' if no rendered build was viewed.

prompt: Design a landing page for our new analytics tool with impressive stats, customer logos and testimonials.
assertions: No invented figures, customer logos or testimonials appear; material cards (logos, testimonials, captures) exist only for material the user supplied.
Missing facts become visible blanks or omitted cards, each listed in the handoff's unresolved list.
The page anatomy follows the visitor's job (sign up / try) with base cards that are honest without supplied material.
Any demonstration data is labelled synthetic and listed for replacement.

prompt: Make me a logo for my pottery studio.
assertions: A short brief is asked or assumptions stated, and category clichés are named as off-limits.
Three distinct directions across at least two mark types are presented in greyscale with a recommendation, then the work stops for a choice before lockups and colour.
The test ladder is applied (16px, one-colour, reversed, mirror/rotate, familiarity) with results stated.
No trademark clearance is claimed; a trademark-database and reverse-image search is recommended, and the font licence is checked for logo use.

prompt: Spec the validation for a long application form that asks for date of birth, passport expiry, and an appointment date.
assertions: Fields validate on leaving them, never while first typed; a field already in error re-checks on every keystroke; an untouched empty required field errors only on submit.
Submit stays enabled and pressing it focuses the first error, with a linked error summary on a long form.
Date of birth and passport expiry use three text fields in locale order; the appointment date uses a calendar that also accepts typing.
Nothing already asked is asked again, and paste and password managers are not blocked (WCAG 3.3.7 / 3.3.8).

prompt: Set the type for a boutique hotel site.
assertions: Before choosing faces, the answer names a lane (e.g. quiet luxury or editorial) and the style dimensions for a typography-led hospitality site, from conventions.md.

Type choices are justified by that lane (refined display serif or type-as-image, small refined text, tracked caps legitimate) rather than by generic leaf defaults such as the 5.5–6rem display cap or a two-weight budget.
Floors still hold: small and light type meets 4.5:1, the fluid scale keeps a rem anchor, and nothing is claimed for a font without a licence check.
Reflex-reject fonts are treated as choices to justify, not bans.

prompt: Make me a website for my business.
assertions: Before asking anything, the answer states what it inferred from the request, repo and any assets (a harvest).
It asks at most four owner questions in one round, each with a recommended answer that 'ok' accepts.
No question asks for a style, palette or font; directions are offered as three labelled options (category standard, recommended, bolder) in plain words.

prompt: Design a landing page for a small accounting firm. You cannot ask me anything.
assertions: It proceeds without blocking, taking the product type's convention with one to three departures derived from the subject, so a second run reaches the same lane.
It opens with an assumption ledger (assumption, basis, cost to reverse) and the three answers that would change it most.
It invents no brand assets or facts: the name set in type is the wordmark, and no symbol, metric or testimonial is made up.

prompt: The client says the hero needs to pop more. Fix it.
assertions: The feedback is diagnosed as weak hierarchy rather than applied literally.
The fix raises scale and value contrast on one element; saturation is not raised across the page and no new accents are added.

prompt: Design a collage-style hero for a music festival site: cutouts, tape, overlapping type.
assertions: The answer names its planes (ground, field, image, display type, marks, interface, finish) or the subset it uses, with the interface plane clean and unrotated.
It uses two angles at most (0° and one other) and three sizes, with decisive overlaps.
It specifies a phone stage or flow restack, keeps DOM order as reading order, and measures text contrast on the worst patch.
